To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mean intercept length of a large number of overlapping grains is not represented by an ellipse, and hence the standard definition of a mean intercept length tensor is not valid.

(i) for anisotropic microstructures the mean intercept length (MIL) is not a second‐rank symmetric tensor, (ii) the MIL tensor is based on a least‐square model fit that is prone to systematic errors, and (iii) the MIL tensor cannot be used to quantify the remnant microstructure anisotropy that is not captured by the MIL.

the mean intercept length, which is commonly used in the analysis of porous microstructures, does not represent a second‐rank anisotropy tensor, and that a robust, comprehensive and systematic alternative is the family of Minkowski tensors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the shape and anisotropy properties of microstructures can be quantified.

the development of a new generation of sensitive structure‐property relations, based on the Minkowski tensor approach, which will allow for the prediction of material properties from structural geometry.
the development and analysis of a new method to quantify anisotropy and its relation to material properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Minkowski tensor analysis is a more robust and comprehensive method to characterize the shape of porous media than the mean‐intercepts length analysis.
the mean intercept length method is useful and informative, but not always reliable, and that the Minkowski tensor method is a promising alternative.
mean‐intercept analysis should only be applied to microstructures that are isotropic in a strict sense, i.e., where the mean intercept length does not depend on the orientation of the test line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mean intercept length method, as it is commonly understood and applied, has conceptual shortcomings.
the Minkowski functionals and the Minkowski tensor analysis are the most general and robust measures for the quantification of the geometry of anisotropic structures.
, while the mean‐intercepts are a useful measure of anisotropies, the mean‐intercep length tensor is an inaccurate measure of the shape of the anisotropic structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MIL tensor is not a robust and accurate measure of the shape of the structure.
the MIL tensor analysis is based on a fundamental model mismatch and hence has conceptual shortcomings.
the mean‐intercepts length analysis is based on a conceptual mismatch between the model assumptions of the mean‐ intercept length tensor and the underlying microstructure.
